notes: Check batch 2026-11-05-check-3: four skill runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus run, all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier (each transcript's assistant messages name only that tier's model). All four ran at head 9a47da2 with uncommitted true and one skill_hash (558f46e4...); skills_listed 40 (haiku-1) and 62 (the others). Every transcript contains the committed new sentences ("Different failures need different reasons too", "the `case` goes in a small private function", "when the success row calls on") and the uncommitted ones ("whose failure already has the shape", "Enum.find_value(pairs"), so the runs read the current working-tree text. Reads: SKILL.md only in all four. Expected reads is none beyond SKILL.md, so all four meet it. In the scratch folder all four files pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors (Elixir 1.20.3). Doctests: haiku-1 1 of 1, haiku-2 1 of 1, sonnet-1 2 of 3, sonnet-2 3 of 3.

Changed rules: git diff 74112b4 -- idiomatic-elixir/ (commits since 74112b4 plus the uncommitted working tree the runs read) changes three of the ten graded rules. Match every expected shape adds "Different failures need different reasons too: a caller cannot tell a missing field from a bad number when both return `{:error, :invalid}`." It decides nothing here: all four runs return :invalid_payload, {:unsupported_event, type}, {:missing_field, key} and {:invalid_field, key} as distinct reasons (verified); sonnet-2 is violated under the unchanged catch-all text. Chain fallible steps adds, committed, "when that call does not return `{:ok, value}`, the `case` goes in a small private function" and, uncommitted, "Give each step a private function whose failure already has the shape the function returns, `{:error, reason}` for a function that returns tuples, `:error` for a fetch, `nil` for a lookup that returns a value or `nil`" with the guard-step sentence "A step that returns a value or `nil` matches with a guard". Neither decides anything: every with step is a private function returning {:ok, _} or {:error, _}, no step returns :error or nil, no case is nested in a with body, and each DateTime.from_unix/1 case sits in its own private function. Inline `->` clauses adds "That pair stays inline because both rows return a value; when the success row calls on, as `{:ok, bytes} -> hash_if_canonical(token, bytes)` does beside `_other -> :error`, the clauses are not a table and every body goes below." Every inline row in haiku-1 and sonnet-2 returns a tuple and no success row calls on, so it holds them clean and decides no violation. The other changes (the Formatting bullet, the and/or rule, the do: rule's == sentence, the Enum.find_value table row, references/ecto-phoenix.md) are outside this case's list and decide nothing: no run writes &&, ||, Enum.find or Ecto code, and haiku-2's `value != ""` (line 158) already puts the checked value on the left. All other verdicts are held to the 2026-10-31-b standard.

Closest calls. The `->` rule: haiku-1 line 182 is exactly 70 characters after the indentation, held clean as 2026-10-31-b held the same 70-character clause; sonnet-2's longest inline clause is 67 (line 172). Match every expected shape: sonnet-2 line 135 defp parse_data(_payment_type, data), do: parse_payment(data) is the catch-all 2026-10-31 graded violated in skill-sonnet-1 and 2026-11-05-check in skill-sonnet-2; haiku-2's parse_data/2 (lines 120-122) names all three atoms and is clean. The non-string type reaching {:unsupported_event, 123} in haiku-1 and haiku-2 (their guards read id and data, not type) is kept in checks, as 2026-10-31-b and 2026-11-05-check did; the reason carries the value, so the new different-reasons sentence does not turn it into a violation. Read required keys: haiku-1's Map.get (line 173) and haiku-2's data["customer_email"] and data["failure_reason"] (lines 132-133) read fields Payment leaves out of @enforce_keys, so optional. Comments: sonnet-1's wrong doctest timestamp ~U[2024-09-22 09:46:40Z] is the same one 2026-10-31-b counted in sonnet-1; the transcript shows its doctest attempts blocked ("The BEAM file of the module cannot be accessed"), and its final message says it could not run them. Naming: haiku-1's object/2 and Event.object field, haiku-2's object variable, and sonnet-1's and sonnet-2's details, reason and email not counted, as kind, payload and details were before; haiku-2's required/3 returns {:error, _} and is named by its job, not fetch. Multi-clause: haiku-1's object/2 and haiku-2's parse_data/2 take data as a positional argument, not a field bound from a matched value. Outside the list: haiku-2's if inside a case (lines 149-151) goes under Keep functions short, as 2026-10-31-b counted haiku-2's same shape; its if ..., do: ..., else: has plain branches and is fine under the do: rule. sonnet-1's {:ok, / %Payment{...}} (lines 162-168) is a return value, not a call argument, not counted under Build a multi-line argument as before; haiku-1's object/2 and sonnet-1's parse_data/2 mix a do: clause with block clauses whose bodies do not fit on the head's line, not counted as before.

Probe of 28 payloads (the three known types, an unknown type, a non-string and a missing type, missing, nil, string and negative amount, missing and nil currency, missing customer_email and payment_id, payment.failed without and with an integer failure_reason, refunds missing refund_id or payment_id, a refund with a string amount, a string and an out-of-range created, missing created, missing and non-string id, missing and list data, a string and a nil payload), run in the scratch folder against each compiled file; nothing raises. In all four: both payment types parse; an unknown type gives {:unsupported_event, "invoice.paid"}; a known type without amount gives {:missing_field, "amount"}, not unsupported; a nil, string or negative amount gives {:invalid_field, "amount"}; a missing currency or payment_id names that field; refunds without refund_id or payment_id name that field; a string or out-of-range created gives {:invalid_field, "created"}; a payload missing type, id, created or data, a non-string id, list data, or a non-map payload gives :invalid_payload. Differences: the refund with only refund_id and payment_id parses in three runs and gives {:missing_field, "amount"} in haiku-1, whose Refund requires amount and currency (it parses when both are present; its final message states the assumption); "type" => 123 gives {:unsupported_event, 123} in haiku-1 and haiku-2 and :invalid_payload in the Sonnet runs; a missing customer_email is rejected only by sonnet-1; payment.failed without failure_reason is rejected by haiku-1 and sonnet-1; "failure_reason" => 5 is accepted only by haiku-2, which reads it with brackets and does not check it; a string refund amount is rejected only by haiku-1, since the other Refunds have no amount.

Compared with the previous skill sweep (2026-10-31-b at 74112b4, Haiku and Sonnet tiers only, since this batch has no opus run): Match every expected shape moves from Sonnet clean to violated (sonnet-2's parse_data(_payment_type, data) catch-all); Comments stays Sonnet violated (the same wrong doctest timestamp in sonnet-1). The other eight rules stay clean in both tiers. Compared with 2026-11-05-check at d593bcb: Haiku moves from violated to clean on Naming (no fetch_field), Comments (no restating comments) and the `->` rule (no success row that calls on); Sonnet moves from clean to violated on Comments; Match every expected shape stays Sonnet violated. None of these moves follows from a text change, since the changed sentences decide no verdict here; with two runs per tier they are differences between runs.
